Matchstick Puzzles Rules

Move one or two matches to make a sum right or to make squares.

The rules

Moving
Tap a match: you pick it up, and a dashed frame shows where it lay. Then tap a free place (a dotted line) to lay it there; tapping its old place puts it back. Above the matches you see how many lie away from their start place.
Sums
The digits are made of matches as on a digital clock. The sign has two places: with both matches it is a plus, with only the lying one a minus. At the end every digit and sign must have a valid shape and the sum must be right. Numbers of two or more digits do not start with 0.
Squares
The figure is made of small squares. Make exactly as many small squares as the task asks; every match must be part of at least one of them - no match may lie loose.
Levels
Easy: sums of single digits with 1 match; squares with 1 or 2 matches. Medium: sums with two-digit numbers, 1 match; squares with 2 matches. Hard: sums with 2 matches; squares with 2 matches and at most two solutions. 30 puzzles per level; the computer has checked that each can be solved with exactly that number of matches and not with fewer. Solved puzzles get a tick in the list.
Hint
Hint marks a match and the place where it should go. Undo takes back the last step; Start over lays all matches back.

Example

Move 1 match: 9 + 3 = 6 is wrong. Take the top right match of the 9 - it becomes a 5 - and lay it on the 6, which becomes an 8: 5 + 3 = 8.
